title: Sharp Flow can never score a single row: the ledger keys movements by Sleeper player id, the board looks them up by displayName
claimUnderTest: config/consensus_edge/params_v1.json gives sharpFlow weight 0.30 and lists it as a coreComponent; src/consensus_edge/inputs.py says it 'degrades to None rather than to a neutral zero' when there is no ledger, implying it works when there IS one. The container's empty ledger is the pre-declared reason the component is dark.
observed: The component is dark for a second, permanent reason that a populated ledger does not fix. inputs.sharp_movements() selects asset_movements.asset_id — which src/intel/ledger.py::ingest writes verbatim from the crawler's `assetId`, i.e. a Sleeper player id such as '12530' or a 'pick:' string — and sharp_flow.movements_from_ledger_rows keys the returned dict by that id. service.build_board then reads `(flow['assets'] or {}).get(key)` where `key` is the fair-value index key, which fair_value._row_key defines as `displayName`. The two key spaces never intersect and no identity join is applied (identity_join.py maps only gsis ids and playerctx). Fed 2,400 synthetic-but-correctly-shaped movements covering 400 of the board's players, sharp_flow_index scores all 400 assets (e.g. asset '12530' -> direction +0.7345) and build_board attaches sharpFlow to 0 of 1092 rows. The board then reports sharpFlowStatus 'ok' alongside componentAvailability.sharpFlow.unavailableReason 'no_data' — a misdiagnosis, since the data was present and it was the join that failed. Keying the identical movements by displayName instead attaches sharpFlow to 400 rows, which isolates the key space as the sole cause.

title: 28 of the board's 73 buy-side rows are labelled Buy directly above their own text saying the fair value is BELOW the market
claimUnderTest: mispricing.py: 'Sign convention: positive means underpriced — our fair value is above the market, so the player is a buy.' The page's subtitle is 'Where our anchor-free fair value disagrees with the market.'
observed: The component score is a cohort-relative z-score, `tanh((logGap - cohortMedian) / cohortSigma / 3)`, so its sign tracks the gap RELATIVE TO the cohort median, not the gap itself. On the live board the anchor-free cohort medians are strongly negative — RB_WR_TE|mid median logGap -0.1688 (the anchor-free board prices the median mid-value skill player 15.5% below KTC), RB_WR_TE|high -0.0755, QB|mid -0.0545 — because removing ktcSfTep + fantasyNavigatorSf shifts the blend's level, not because the market is wrong. A player at -6% is therefore +0.99 sigma and scores +30.7, which classify() turns into 'Buy'. 28 of the 325 scored rows land this way, i.e. 28 of the 73 buy-side labels (38%). Each such row's `explanation[0]`, rendered verbatim at page.jsx:306, reads e.g. 'Our anchor-free fair value is 6% below the market (1594 vs 1702).' immediately under the word 'Buy'. Nothing in the payload, the page, or the 25 ADRs in docs/consensus-edge/DECISIONS.md states that the score is cohort-relative rather than absolute, or that the displayed pctGap is dominated by a level artifact.

userImpact: A user reading the buy list acquires players the model's own fair value says are worth LESS than the asking price. The row's own sentence contradicts its own label, so there is no way to tell whether the label or the sentence is the mistake. Because the cohort medians differ by tier (elite +0.0269, mid -0.1688), the effect is systematic: it manufactures buy signals concentrated in the mid tier and suppresses them at the top.
whatWorks: The cohort-conditioned z-score is itself a defensible design and is exactly what de-means the level artifact out of the RANKING — the ordering within a cohort is sound. MAD-based sigma, the smooth tanh saturation replacing the old hard clamp, the specific->family cohort fallback with cohortLevel stamped, and the refusal on cohorts below n=12 all reproduce exactly from the payload.
rootCause: Two quantities are conflated at the surface: an absolute gap (what the explanation prints and what the sign convention promises) and a cohort-relative gap (what the score and label are computed from). They have different signs for 28 rows because the leave-one-out board is not on the same level as the anchor it is compared against, and the classification bands are applied to the relative quantity without ever saying so.
requiredRepair: Either (a) gate a directional label on the absolute gap agreeing in sign with the relative one — a row whose fair value is below market cannot be a Buy — or (b) rewrite the explanation and the sign-convention docstring to state the cohort-relative basis explicitly and print the cohort-excess gap rather than the raw pctGap. Whichever is chosen, record the level shift (the cohort medians) in the payload so a reader can see that the anchor-free board is not level-matched to the anchor.
dependencies: None. Independent of the flag state and of F001/F002.

title: The daily snapshot history that the whole feature is being kept alive to accumulate cannot be verified here, and would record a permanently-dark Sharp Flow
claimUnderTest: src/consensus_edge/inputs.py: both callers — the API and the daily snapshot job — spend the same resolved inputs, so 'the board we record cannot be built from less evidence than the board we serve'.
observed: The shared-inputs invariant does hold structurally (both call inputs.resolve), but it cannot be checked against a real history here: /api/consensus-edge/health reports snapshotStore {"exists": false, "snapshots": 0, "reason": "no snapshot database on disk"} because the snapshot store lives under gitignored data/ and no timer has run in this container. The absent path is the one src/consensus_edge/snapshot.py resolves under data/ (data/consensus_edge/). Two consequences worth stating: the timer is installed unconditionally by deploy/install-systemd-service.sh and runs daily at 07:30 UTC regardless of the feature flag — three full pipeline passes a day for a board no user can see, which is deliberate (the history is the point) but is a standing cost of a switched-off feature; and because the job shares inputs.resolve it inherits W14-F001, so every snapshot it has ever recorded in production carries sharpFlow absent on every row. The invariant is satisfied and both sides are wrong in the same way.

reproduction.expected: a snapshot database with at least one recorded board
reproduction.actual: {'exists': False, 'snapshots': 0, 'reason': 'no snapshot database on disk'}; ls: cannot access 'data/consensus_edge': No such file or directory; the snapshot script contains no feature-flag check

userImpact: None today. It matters for the feature's stated future: the flag is supposed to come back on when a re-run of the gate passes, and that re-run is fed by this history. A history recorded with one of two core components permanently dark cannot validate a composite that weights that component 0.30.
whatWorks: The health endpoint reports the snapshot store's absence explicitly — including the permission-error case — rather than 500ing or omitting the block, which is exactly the visibility a silently-stopped oneshot needs. inputs.py's single-resolution design is the right shape and does prevent the record/serve divergence it was written for.
rootCause: data/consensus_edge/ does not exist in this container; the snapshot timer has never run here.
requiredRepair: Verify on a production host: check snapshotStore.lastDate on /api/consensus-edge/health and confirm the recorded boards carry a non-null sharpFlow once W14-F001 is fixed.
